title: Data Structures & Big-O Complexity
description: Time complexity of common operations on arrays, lists, trees, heaps, and hash tables, each with a one-line reason. Handy for CS courses and interview prep.
subject: computer-science

cards.definition: O(1). Hashing the key jumps straight to its bucket, so the time doesn't grow with the number of entries.

cards.term: Binary search on a sorted array
cards.definition: O(log n). Each comparison discards half of the remaining elements.
O(n log n) on average, O(n²) in the worst case. Consistently bad pivots make the partitions lopsided.
O(1). The element's address is computed directly from the start address and the index.
O(n). If many keys collide into the same bucket, a lookup may have to check every one of them.

cards.term: Linear search in an unsorted array
cards.definition: O(n). With no ordering to exploit, every element may need to be checked.

cards.term: Insert at the front of an array
cards.definition: O(n). Every existing element must shift one position to make room.
O(1). Resizing copies everything, but growing the capacity geometrically makes resizes rare enough to average out.

cards.term: Insert at the head of a singly linked list
cards.definition: O(1). Only the new node's next pointer and the head pointer change.

cards.term: Access the k-th element of a linked list
cards.definition: O(n). There is no direct indexing, so nodes must be followed one by one from the head.
O(1). Both operations touch only the top element.
O(1). With a linked list or circular buffer, both ends are reachable directly.
O(log n). The tree's height stays logarithmic, so a search follows one short root-to-leaf path.

cards.term: Unbalanced binary search tree search (worst case)
cards.definition: O(n). Inserting keys in sorted order can degrade the tree into a single chain.

cards.term: Binary heap peek at min or max
cards.definition: O(1). The smallest (or largest) element always sits at the root.
O(log n). The new element sifts up at most the height of the tree.

cards.term: Binary heap extract min or max
cards.definition: O(log n). The last element moves to the root and sifts down at most the height of the tree.

cards.term: Build a binary heap from n elements
cards.definition: O(n). Bottom-up heapify does most of its work on low nodes, which only sift down a short distance.
O(n log n) in every case. The input is halved about log n times, and each level merges n elements.
O(n). Each element is compared once with its neighbor and never needs to move.
O(V + E) with an adjacency list. Each vertex is visited once and each edge is examined a constant number of times.
O(L), where L is the word's length. One step per character, no matter how many words are stored.
